body: Forward test of the base rate method (NOT a recommendation; not buy/sell). Probability 0.55 (naive base rate 0.62) that: The Virginia State Corporation Commission issues a final order approving (with or without conditions) the NextEra–Dominion combination by 31-Mar-2027. Evidence: NEE Q3 2026 release (Oct-2026): shareholders of both companies approved the combination on 3-Sep-2026; 'In Virginia and South Carolina, procedural schedules have been set with hearings in November and December, respectively, and the companies expect final orders in January 2027'; North Carolina procedural schedule set; a Virginia 'comprehensive benefits package centered around affordability'; closing expected in H2 2027. NEE reaffirmed 2026 adjusted EPS $3.92–4.02 (targeting the high end). Reasoning: Base-rate test: state utility-merger approvals usually come within a couple of months of company-expected dates, but Virginia is the politically hardest state here (data-centre load growth, bill affordability, Dominion's home state), and an SCC order with unacceptable conditions or a delayed schedule is plausible. We shade below the reference class and give two months of slack past January. Resolution: YES if the Virginia SCC issues a final order approving the NextEra Energy–Dominion Energy merger (approval with conditions counts, even if the companies later contest conditions) on or before 31-Mar-2027, per the SCC docket or a company 8-K/press release. A rejection, or no final order by that date, is NO. Source: Virginia SCC case docket / NEE and D 8-K filings. Resolve by 2027-04-15; score with Brier vs base rate.

body: Method-test variant-perception record (not a recommendation). MARKET PRICES: Sunflag as a discounted LMEL proxy - at our steel DCF the post-tax stake carries a 45-61% (central 52%) discount; equivalently, at a 55% discount steel trades at 5.4x EV/EBITDA, 12.5x P/E. OUR VIEW: no claimable mispricing; the discount is explained by no monetisation/payout policy, collateral use of the stake (74 lakh shares pledged), a mining programme with weak delivery, and no investor communication; underweighted by the market: near-zero net debt, AA- rating, ~14% pre-tax operating ROCE. PROVES US WRONG: (a) LMEL sale + buyback/special dividend (gap closes); (b) stake proceeds or new debt into mining, borrowings > Rs 1,000 cr (discount widens); (c) FY27 OPM < 9%. Market-cap/stake ratio on 20-Nov-2026: 0.64 (3-yr range 0.46-1.12).
title: Variant view (live #1): Sunflag's ~50% discount on its LMEL stake is justified and persists absent a distribution event; the steel business is safe, the risk is LMEL
